correctness.rationale: Multiplying the defining reciprocal sum by n and reducing modulo each maximal prime power gives the stated local congruence exactly; for at most four supports a sharp elementary reciprocal bound keeps every positive integral value below 2. The three-support classification follows from an exact reduction to d-1=[Aq-d(r-1)]V and a complete d=1/d>1 case split, with the latter eliminated by size and modulo-3 arguments. Exact-rational verification found zero mismatches among 98,158 tested integers up to 100,000.

originality.rationale: Machacek's foundational paper, OEIS A283423, the μ-Sondow literature, recent primary-pseudoperfect work, exact/synonymous web searches, and the current SCOPE archive were checked. No located source states the prime-power local criterion or the uniqueness of 6*7^c in the three-support middle-exponent-one slice. Originality remains to the best of our knowledge, with residual terminology risk.

value.rationale: The result gives an exact local test for a global Egyptian-fraction integrality condition, upgrades it to a complete criterion for prime power pseudoperfectness through four supports, and proves a converse uniqueness theorem for a natural infinite family previously known constructively.
